title: Causal Effect Identification under Functional Dependence without Positivity in a Four-Node Categorical Model
banked_reason: Field-floor terminal: the graph-general F-ID+ front-end retains an explicit positive-support residual with no identification verdict; the sound categorical four-node theorem achieves subfield tier. review_math also records a local output-bound h^2/degree-2d bookkeeping defect that does not affect the tier verdict.
gap_reasons: The note does not deliver the targeted graph-general complete F-ID+ algorithm: `thm:fixed-alphabet-four-output-front-end` may terminate with `Psi_U` and explicitly makes no identification verdict.
This restriction leaves the headline general object open and caps the contribution at subfield.

The coefficient-height proof drops a product term: (12) contains Q_theta(ell) P_theta(E0), a product of two network polynomials with up to h monomials each, so after simplex substitution its collected coefficients need not be bounded by 2h as claimed.
proof_attempt_summary: The run constructed a graph-general four-output front end and proved exact feasibility, support propagation, guarded success cases, and support-hole countermodels, but the positive-support residual Psi_U still has no identification verdict. It also derived a sound arbitrary-support response-kernel fiber, rational original-alphabet attainment, the B_sat^0 cardinality elbow, sharp single-X projection, joint-positive collapse, and branch-respecting inference for the four-node hidden-functional family. Reaching field tier still requires a cardinality-preserving graph-general converse without generic QE; the local h^2/degree-2d output-bound bookkeeping defect should also be repaired on reuse.
tldr: For the four-node categorical model with hidden non-root \(A=f(Z)\), the observed law has a complete fixed-alphabet solution on every support pattern: count positive-root profiles for feasibility, enumerate augmented hidden-state partitions for the exact full response-kernel region, and project to a product of translated simplexes for intervention on \(X\) alone.  The construction attains every rational selected point with rational original-alphabet mechanisms, identifies the least hidden cardinality at which missing response rows decouple, and collapses to \(P(Y\mid Z,X)\) only under the required joint-support guards.  For general finite DAGs, exact feasibility, guarded sound successes, and exact separating witnesses are available output lanes, but the cardinality-preserving guarded-district success-or-countermodel dichotomy remains open; branch-respecting multinomial inference applies only after a point-identifying guarded leaf has been certified.
gap: Chen--Darwiche Theorem 18 gives a reduction on the broader separate-marginal-positivity domain, but its converse construction may enlarge alphabets and does not impose a total exact output contract; Hwang et al. extract sufficient positivity for returned formulas but prove only soundness of that return guarantee; classical ID, invariant-cut search, and CSI algorithms do not deliver a fixed-alphabet joint-positive success-or-countermodel dichotomy.
fill: The proposed \(\mathsf{F\text{-}ID}^{+}\) architecture combines exact feasibility, reachable-support and algebraic stratification, guarded district recursion, and alphabet-preserving algebraic countermodel compilation, with rational certificates as a preferred special case, a sharp binary boundary theorem, and branch-respecting multinomial inference.
